lines.text: The Trojan Horse isn't in the Iliad.
Homer's Iliad covers just a few weeks of the ten year Trojan War, and it ends with a funeral, not a horse.
The horse gets brief mentions in the Odyssey. The full story comes from the Roman poet Virgil, centuries later.
The Greeks built a giant wooden horse, hid soldiers inside, and pretended to sail away.
A Trojan priest named Laocoon warned: I fear the Greeks, even when they bring gifts. Then two sea serpents killed him.
So the Trojans dragged the horse inside their walls. That night, the soldiers climbed out and opened the gates.
